meta.title: IELTS Academic mock test — computer-delivered format
meta.description: A full IELTS Academic mock in the computer-delivered format: Listening, Reading and Writing, with your band on submit and AI feedback on Writing.

ielts.h1: IELTS Academic mock, in the real computer-delivered format
ielts.sub: Listening, Reading and Writing with the official timing and question types. Listening and Reading are scored on submit; Writing is graded by AI on all four criteria.

faq.a1: Not yet. The full mock covers Listening, Reading and Writing in one sitting (2 hours 40 minutes).
faq.q2: Which question types are in Reading?
faq.a2: True / False / Not Given, multiple choice, matching headings, sentence and summary completion, and the other types used in the computer-delivered test.
faq.q3: How is the overall band worked out?
faq.a3: Each section is scored on the 0–9 band scale in 0.5 steps. The overall band is the average of your Listening, Reading and Writing bands.
faq.q4: Can I take only one section?
faq.a4: Yes. Buy one section, or use your free Listening or Reading section. Writing is a paid section because it is graded by AI.
faq.a1Sp: Yes. Speaking has 3 parts (11–14 minutes): a computer-generated British examiner voice asks the questions, your answers are recorded and AI scores them on 4 criteria. You need a laptop or computer with a microphone. In a full mock you can take Speaking on a separate day within 7 days.
faq.a3Sp: Each section is scored 0–9 in steps of 0.5. The overall band is the average of all four sections (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking); it appears once Speaking is done.
faq.a4Sp: Yes. Buy one section or use the free Listening or Reading section. Writing and Speaking are paid because AI scores them.

ielts.subSp: Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking with official timing and question types. Listening and Reading are scored on submit; Writing and Speaking are scored by AI on four criteria.

meta.title: Digital SAT mock test — Bluebook-style adaptive modules
meta.description: A full Digital SAT mock with two adaptive modules per section, built-in Desmos and a reference sheet. Your total out of 1600 on submit.

sat.h1: Digital SAT mock with adaptive modules, like Bluebook
sat.sub: Reading and Writing, then Math, each in two modules where Module 2 adapts to how you did. Built-in Desmos, reference sheet, annotate and option eliminator.

faq.a1: Yes. Your Module 1 result decides whether Module 2 is the easier or the harder version, as on the real Digital SAT.
faq.a2: Yes. Math has the Desmos graphing calculator and the reference sheet built in.
faq.a3: Yes. A 10-minute break between Reading and Writing and Math, with a countdown.
faq.q4: What does the free section include?
faq.a4: The whole Reading and Writing section, both modules, with your section score and a review of every question.

common.previewSub: The same question styles you meet in the exam. Exam content is always in English.
common.ctaBody: Start with one free section. No card needed.

meta.title: How Eduvo Mock works
meta.description: Choose IELTS or SAT, sit the mock in the real computer-based interface, get your score on submit and AI Writing feedback, then practise what you missed.

how.sub: From sign-up to a result you can act on, in four steps.

scoring.lText: Marked automatically the moment you submit. Your band comes from the number of correct answers, using the IELTS conversion.
scoring.wText: Graded by AI on Task Achievement or Response, Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource and Grammatical Range and Accuracy, usually within minutes.
scoring.sText: Each section is scored from your answers in both modules; the total is out of 1600.
